name_note: GTDB divides the classical genus Roseburia into several genera, of which g__Roseburia_C is one, so the cited literature on Roseburia covers a broader group than this GTDB genus.

sentences.text: Roseburia is a genus of obligate Gram-positive anaerobic bacteria that are slightly curved, rod-shaped and motile by multiple subterminal flagella.
Gut Roseburia species metabolize dietary components and are described as commensal bacteria producing short-chain fatty acids, especially butyrate.
A review reports that modification in Roseburia representation is associated with several diseases, including irritable bowel syndrome, obesity and type 2 diabetes.
A human study reported a strong association between low scores on an alcohol use screening test and the abundance of the genus Roseburia.
A study of colorectal cancer patients reported that sequence clusters belonging to the genus Roseburia and other butyrate-producing Lachnospiraceae were less abundant than in healthy volunteers.
